The problem

Linter output is factual. Actionability is contextual.

Intent matters

A multi-resource policy, enforcement default, or missing-property check may be deliberate.

Findings overlap

Optional aliases, old API versions, and repeated paths often describe one underlying decision.

Automation needs structure

PR pipelines need stable IDs, pointers, source indexes, and bounded actions rather than prose.

What the skill does

One policy. One result set. One structured triage.

Strict JSON

Action model

Separate safe edits from policy decisions.

direct_edit

The policy alone determines a semantics-preserving change.

choice_required

The author must choose among bounded behavioral or assignment-contract options.

investigate

Provider behavior, API usage, stale input, or another external fact is required.

none

The concern is disproven, already handled, or irrelevant to the policy's role.

Reviewed semantic performance is 39/40 on eight mechanically gradable refined cases. It is a sensitivity result, not a replacement for the frozen primary rubric.

What improved

The skill now handles the hard edges explicitly.

  • Critical findings block incomplete triage.
  • Property-bag paths resolve against the supplied root.
  • Console metadata loss produces partial results.
  • Stale paths become low-confidence investigations.
  • Assignment-interface changes require author choice.
  • Evidence and target pointers have tighter membership rules.

Remaining risk

Correctness is strong. Exact repetition is not.

39/40

Reviewed semantic passes after rubric corrections.

17/80

Exact structural pair agreement in the refined affected cases.

Aggregation boundaries, confidence, evidence pointers, and alternatives can vary. Consumers should trust the schema and stable IDs, not require byte-for-byte identical analyses.

ADO integration

A mirrored file is not an automatically loaded skill.

Why it is not discovered

The ADO PRAssistant loads explicit prompts and supplied PR context. Mirroring preserves repository content, but it does not register that content with the assistant's skill loader or inject linter JSON.

How to integrate it

Teach the PRAssistant pipeline to load the mirrored skill and schema, then pass the selected policy and linter JSON into that prompt before creating review comments.

The likely integration point is the Policy repository's PRBuiltInPolicy_Linter pipeline, not the repository mirror itself.
